title: Plan §10's literal grep checklist over-fires on legitimate contrastive prose; interpreted by intent, not letter
detail: The checklist items `grep -ri "nestjs|fastify|postgres|docker|turbo"` (expect 0 outside plan §0.0) and `grep -ri "appointment|dealership|technician" apps/ packages/ docs/ directives/` (expect 0) both fire on docs/directives that legitimately explain what was rejected and why (e.g. "no Docker, no turbo" in docs/09_running_it.md; "Scenario 01 pushed its own correctness guarantee (no two overlapping appointments) into..." in docs/adr/0001). None of the hits reintroduce the actual technology or business domain — they are all cross-references to ../service-appointment-scheduler/ or explanations of an omission. Treated as satisfying the checklist's intent (nothing actually uses NestJS/Postgres/Docker/Turbo; nothing reintroduces dealership/technician domain vocabulary as a modeled concept) rather than its literal zero-hits wording. Documented here rather than silently accepted.

title: A partial PATCH on Shift needs a merged-state guard beyond Zod -- InvalidShiftTimeRangeError, not a second validator
detail: createShiftSchema/updateShiftSchema's .refine(endMinute > startMinute) only sees the PATCH BODY, not the existing row -- a request patching only { endMinute: 100 } against an existing { startMinute: 600, endMinute: 900 } passes Zod's refine trivially (startMinute is undefined in the patch) but would merge into an invalid overnight range if written through unchecked. UpdateShiftHandler merges the patch with the existing row and checks endMinute > startMinute itself, throwing InvalidShiftTimeRangeError (422) if violated -- same domain-constraint class as FeasibilityGate (enforced on already-well-typed data), not a second input validator; directives/zod_validation.md's rule 4 governs REQUEST validation, not a check that needs the existing DB row to evaluate. Verified live against Postgres: PATCH {endMinute:100} on a {600,900} shift returns 422 INVALID_SHIFT_TIME_RANGE, not a silently corrupted row.

title: Cross-scenario audit rule: process/convention directives must be diffable against the sibling scenario and differ ONLY in fill-in slots; business/domain docs may differ freely
detail: User's rule, stated explicitly: documents that are business-specific may differ between scenarios, but shared process/coding-architecture/testing/convention documents must stay the same. Enforced this pass by literally diffing every shared file between service-appointment-scheduler and demand-driven-staff-scheduler rather than reading each in isolation -- which is what surfaced the drift a per-file read had missed twice: memory_sop.md had silently DROPPED two things (the 'observability' routing-table category, and the whole 'see .ai/memory for real examples / this is AI-collaboration evidence' paragraph); cqrs_pattern.md had dropped the 'Response DTOs are FLAT' placement rule; qa_standard.md told the reader to run `npm run typecheck && npm run lint` when this repo has the same `npm run check` script scenario 01's copy names; testing_standard.md still described layer 3 as 'apps/web, real SQLite file' and prescribed a Vitest `vi.fn()` mocking pattern while apps/scheduler-api/eslint.config.mjs cross-references this very file for the Jest `jest.Mocked<T>` pattern. Also normalized STYLE: my earlier 'Reconciled to the real two-app shape (Phase F...)' headers read as changelog entries; scenario 01's convention is a terse 3-5 line provenance note saying what was ported/trimmed and why. Changelog belongs in .ai/PROJECT_STATUS.md, not in a rule file. Rule going forward: `diff ../<other-scenario>/directives/<file> directives/<file>` is part of finishing any edit to a shared directive -- remaining diff lines should be only domain examples and commands.

title: ../_templates/directives/ now holds all 13 common directives with a mandatory `<!-- TEMPLATE ... SPECIALIZE: ... -->` header, not just the 3 I first judged templatable
detail: Earlier I argued only memory_sop/qa_standard/cqrs_pattern were templatable and that naming_conventions/domain_modeling/zod_validation/testing_standard were 'correctly scenario-specific'. That was wrong in the same direction as the missing-directives bug: those files' RULES are shared (groups 4-9 of naming_conventions are the Repository/CQRS/error/module families; zod_validation §4 is identical everywhere), only their examples differ. Every template now carries a header naming exactly what to specialize, and the folder README states the non-negotiables: don't delete a rule that doesn't apply (mark ⏸ + trigger), verify Prisma major version before copying database_standard (5 vs 7 need opposite datasource shapes), and port a real fix back to the template in the SAME task. Two verification commands are documented there and were run this session: (1) grep every `directives/*.md` path referenced in code/docs and assert the file exists -- this is what would have caught the five absences years earlier; (2) diff section HEADINGS between two scenarios' copies -- structural difference = drift, content difference = fine. After this pass, heading-diff vs scenario 01 is 0 for memory_sop/qa_standard/cqrs_pattern/logging_standard/observability_monitoring and the remaining 2-4 line diffs in resilience/idempotency/folder_structure/database are all intentional and self-documenting (scenario name, Prisma version, not-built status).
